fun_highlights: The callback architecture is the game's best surprise engine. When Beatrix Okonkwo (Dynasty 4, gen 4) reaches middle age and the 'looked-away' child callback fires — 'A figure in a doorway, hunched against the cold, and she feels the decades fold: the same averted glance' — it lands as a genuine surprise because it reaches back to a specific young-life choice. The lookaway -> cb_lookaway arc and the 'child books -> cb_books_late -> gave the book to a young one' arc at age 47 in the same life are the clearest evidence the engine can be unpredictable.

The c_origin card is doing real work. The same structural beat (early years) produces wildly different prose depending on era, seat, and traits: Hale Okonkwo (Dynasty 4, gen 5) opens under plague dread; Calla Okonkwo (Dynasty 4, gen 1) opens in settled ordinary years; Beatrix opens in a lean-time house. Reading five consecutive gen-1 founders and finding the childhood opener different each time is a genuine anti-staleness win.

Sudden early deaths (Joaquin Castellane at 16, Linnea Brandt at 18, Theda Brandt at 10) are effective jolts. They refuse the expected arc and reframe the next life as an unexpected heir carrying those 'gone too soon' stories. The 'was born a cousin to the line that mattered' collateral succession framing adds texture the domestic arc lacks.

The era layer tilts what is possible in a life. The war-era marriage prompt ('there is a war on, and they have stopped pretending the future is guaranteed') produces a more charged version of a beat the player has seen many times. Small, but it stops the marriage card from feeling purely mechanical every time.

The 'make a name' reputation-choice card (a_make_name) and the 'family shadow' card (r_family_shadow) are the dynasty layer's best surprises: they make the player feel that what their ancestors DID is now creating different encounters. The Castellane motto 'By our own hands' crystallising at the end of Caleb's generation (Dynasty 7) then shaping Otto and Lucan's opening lines feels like a genuine through-line the player can be surprised to encounter.

The bequest mechanic is structurally clever. Anders Lindqvist (Dynasty 13, gen 5) choosing 'Nothing but their own freedom' and the heir screen registering that choice with 'From Anders, deliberately: nothing but your own freedom — no weight, no debt, no map' is a direct player-action surprise landing in a future life.
staleness: The 'began from nothing / laid the first course' card (s_from_nothing) fires with mechanical regularity in nearly every low-seat life. In the transcripts: Saoirse Holloway at 33, Cassian Achterberg at 29, Ottilie Ashby at 40, Noor Okonkwo at (implicit), Mira Halloran at 45, Emory Lindqvist at 53, Ronja Brandt at 32. The prose rotates ('Build, brick by brick' / 'Find others to climb with') but the card itself is predictable enough that reading it no longer produces any surprise. The age-gate is wide (26-54) and the cond (seat<=1) stays true for most of these lives, so it keeps surfacing as a structural beat.

The 'body sends its first real letter' health card (m_health) is visible in almost every long life. Saoirse at 51, Elias at 45, Noor at 73, Henrik at 67, Tomas at 67, Selma at 62, Cassian Thorne at 43, Ingrid at 70, Annika Brandt at 62. The prose rotates but the stakes-framing is identical: a scare, a doctor, 'change everything or carry on.' By life six it is pure clockwork. It fires once per life (onceDyn:4 gives only mild spacing across generations), so readers with a multi-dynasty session hit it on roughly the same schedule.

The ambient observe() lines for high-mind or high-spirit congeal into predictable wallpaper. 'Books have become a country they can live in,' 'There is a whole life they keep behind the eyes,' 'Thinking has become their favourite weather,' and 'She has accumulated, quietly, an interior the size of a small country' appear in Dynasty 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, and 15. The obsPick pool is large but the per-life cap (P._obsN <= 4) means a long-lived scholar hits a ceiling of four ambient obs per life, and the same THEMES (body/mind/means) appear in roughly the same order every long life regardless of which exact line fires.

The 'what do you want to be remembered for' elder card (e_legacy) fires in a very large fraction of long lives, and the three-option structure ('kind / built / here at all') is instantly recognisable once seen twice. In Dynasty 4: Hale and Beatrix both face it. In Dynasty 7: Caleb and Annika both face it. In Dynasty 13: Anders Aldecott and Tobias Aldecott both face it. The prompt varies by vocation but the choices are fixed; a player who has seen it once knows exactly what is coming.

The 'age of the road / wander to stay' elder summing-up beats repeat their structure almost verbatim. 'The road is mostly behind them now; the body has called them in for good. All those places, all that going — it asks to be added up' appears in Hale Okonkwo, Ingrid Thorne, Cleo Castellane, Tobias Aldecott, and Anders Lindqvist. The choices ('Regret nothing' vs 'Count the doors you closed') are the same every time. Being a wanderer practically guarantees this beat, and because wanderer is a common calling, it recurs in near-identical form across unrelated dynasties.

The grief-at-work beat ('Lost someone to the war and put the loss away in work, where it kept, badly, for years') fires with the exact same flavour text in Elias Okonkwo (age 38), Noor Okonkwo (age 53), and Caleb Castellane (age 47). The prose is literally identical: 'Bury it in work. Keep moving.' vs 'Let the grief in.' The war-era gates this card, but since the era rotates to war often enough and the same two-choice structure plus identical log line recurs verbatim, it registers as template repetition rather than a genuine new moment.

improvements.what: Break s_from_nothing into at least two structurally different cards gated by context — one for founders (no name, first generation), one for heirs who fell back to nothing, with distinct prose and stakes. The current card's range (age 26-54, seat<=1) catches wildly different life situations and gives them the same template.
improvements.why: It appears in 7+ of 15 dynasties often as a structural anchor around age 28-40, which makes every low-seat adulthood feel like it passes through the same doorway regardless of who the person is or what came before. A founder starting from nothing is a different dramatic situation than an heir who fell from something.

improvements.what: Give the body/health cards (m_health, e_body) a vocation-specific variant text pool or a memory-gated twist — so a soldier's body scare reads differently from a scholar's, and a character who already pushed the body once (peril flag) gets a harder, more personal prompt the second time.
improvements.why: The health card is the single most clockwork beat in the transcripts. It appears in nearly identical form across vocations and generations. The existing prose pool is good but the STRUCTURE (doctor, scare, word to look up) does not vary. A soldier who took peril at 25 should face this beat with different framing than a bookish scholar who never once risked the body.

improvements.what: Tighten the onceDyn cooldown on the wanderer-summing-up beat (the 'road is mostly behind them' text block inside e_bequest and the wanderer elder arc) so the same philosophical framing cannot repeat in consecutive dynasties even in different characters. Right now the wanderer calling reliably produces the same reckoning structure every time a wanderer lives past 65.
improvements.why: Four of the five wanderer elders in the transcripts face virtually identical summing-up language. The player can anticipate the beat the moment vocation='wanderer' is set.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 genuinely unexpected negative-space events: moments that do NOT fit the five-vocation template and cannot be predicted from the character's established trajectory. Examples: a life-shaping accident of mistaken identity; a moment where the house's reputation causes an unexpected problem rather than a door opening; a quiet absurd windfall completely incongruent with the life's tone. Right now every life is legible from its calling + era combination.
improvements.why: The surprise_hunter lens reveals that the entire card space is coherently organised around calling, era, and stat bands. That coherence is good architecture but it means a player who understands the system can predict 80% of what is coming. True surprise requires at least some events that feel slightly orthogonal to the life's established logic.

improvements.what: Deepen the dynasty-layer callbacks: make the house reputation produce encounters that CONTRADICT or complicate the reputation rather than only reward it. A 'kind' house should eventually face a moment where kindness is weaponised against it (someone exploits the open door); a 'ruthless' house should face a moment of unexpected softness from someone who remembers them differently. The current reputation-gated cards (r_scholar_door, r_family_shadow) mostly confirm what the house already is.
improvements.why: The heir screen's 'of a family known as kind-hearted' framing raises player expectations that the reputation will create varied encounters. But in practice the reputation mostly affects which optional door appears rather than the texture of the ordinary day. Contradiction would be a stronger surprise driver than confirmation.

verdict: A Life has genuine surprise infrastructure — the callback architecture (books, lookaway, talent, first-loss) delivers moments that feel earned by earlier choices, and the era/seat/trait system makes the same structural beat read differently across lives. But reading 15 dynasties reveals that the skeleton is too predictable: a medium-length life of any vocation will almost certainly pass through s_from_nothing, a health scare, a legacy question, and a body-summing-up in roughly that order, with near-identical language. The game's strongest moments are the ones that reach BACK (the looked-away child at 49, the old book re-read at 50); the weakest are the structural milestones that every life hits on schedule regardless of who the person is. At this density the session feels less like witnessing a unique life and more like watching a template populate — the surprise_hunter leaves impressed by the writing quality but underwhelmed by the frequency of genuine unpredictability.
